title: Default include_context to true when reply_to is sender
description:
Currently include_context defaults to false. When reply_to is 'sender' (the default), the peer gets no context about what we're discussing, so it can't give informed answers.

Fix: when reply_to is 'sender' and include_context is not explicitly set, auto-enable context inclusion. This makes the 'ask a question' use case work out of the box.

Discovered when testing silent mode — peer said 'I'm not working on anything' because it had zero context.
close_reason: Fixed: include_context now auto-enables when reply_to is 'sender' (the default). Explicit false still works to opt out.

title: Crash on disconnect when peer already cleaned up link dir
description:
When one side disconnects and cleans up the link directory, the other side crashes with ENOENT if writeMeta is called (e.g. from a queued heartbeat or during disconnect cleanup).

Stack trace:
  error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '~/.pi/links/<id>/meta.json'
    at writeMeta (types.ts:98:19)

Fix: make writeMeta tolerant of missing directories — catch ENOENT and silently ignore. Already applied.

Root cause: cleanup() only the host removes the dir, but the guest may still have a heartbeat callback queued that fires after the host's cleanup. Race condition between stopHeartbeat() and the event loop.

title: Persistent links across session reload
description:
Currently /reload kills UDS connections. Links should survive by storing peer metadata in the session and reconnecting on session_start.

Changes:
- Store link info (linkId, mode, peer session) in session state
- On session_start, check for stored links and attempt reconnect
- If reconnect fails, notify user but don't crash
- /link status shows recovery state

title: Cross-machine links via A2A/ACP HTTP adapter
description:
Implemented HTTP adapter for cross-machine linking:

types.ts:
- Added HTTP_LINK_DEFAULT_PORT (4567), HTTP_LINK_SECRET_FILE, HTTP_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS (5min)
- Added transport field to LinkState (uds|http)
- Added httpServer, httpPort, httpRemoteUrl, httpSecret fields to LinkState
- Added getLinkSecret/ensureLinkSecret helpers (env var or ~/.pi/links/shared-secret)
- Added httpPostRpc helper for HTTP-based JSON-RPC calls

index.ts:
- HTTP server with auth (Bearer token), discovery (/.well-known/agent.json), health (/health), RPC (/rpc)
- handleHttpRpc: synchronous task processing over HTTP (silent tasks return result inline, visible tasks get ack)
- connectHttpRemote: guest connects to remote HTTP endpoint, discovers agent card, verifies with ping
- /link create --http [port]: starts HTTP adapter alongside UDS server
- /link http://host:port: connect to remote link via HTTP
- /link list: shows active link + all local UDS links
- link_send_task: uses HTTP transport when connected via HTTP (synchronous response)
- Widget shows [HTTP] or [HTTP :port] for HTTP connections
- cmdStatus shows transport type and HTTP-specific info
- link_status tool includes transport, httpPort, httpRemoteUrl

Auth: Shared secret via PI_LINK_SECRET env var or ~/.pi/links/shared-secret file (auto-generated)

title: Multi-link support
description:
Implemented multi-link support:

Core refactor:
- linksRegistry Map stores all active links (keyed by link ID)
- state variable points to the active link for backward compatibility
- Per-link functions take explicit LinkState parameter (handleDataForLink, handleMsgForLink, etc.)
- Closures in cmdCreate/cmdJoin capture specific link state, not global state
- setActiveLink/getActiveLink for active link management
- removeLink auto-promotes next connected link to active

New features:
- /link list shows all links with index, transport, status, peer info
- /link disconnect [id|index] disconnects specific link
- link_send_task target parameter: resolves by ID prefix, session name, peer name, or index
- Widget shows all links when multiple active (single link uses compact display)
- link_status tool returns array of all links with active flag
- Version bumped to v0.2.0

Recovery updated:
- session_shutdown persists all links for recovery
- agent_end checks all links for pending visible tasks

title: Streaming results via task/stream
description:
Implemented streaming results via task/stream:

headless.ts:
- Added optional onChunk callback to runSilentTask
- Captures content_block_delta events from pi subprocess JSON output
- When streaming, builds lastAssistantText from deltas (avoids double-count with message_end)
- When not streaming, falls back to message_end content (unchanged behavior)

index.ts:
- task/stream message handler: receives chunks, accumulates in streamBuffers map
- Stream widget: shows last 300 chars of streaming content with task ID
- Widget auto-clears when stream completes (done=true) or all streams finish
- processSilentTaskForLink: sends chunks as JSON-RPC task/stream notifications when stream=true
- Sends done signal after task completion
- link_send_task stream parameter: enables streaming for UDS transport
- When streaming, tool doesn't terminate (waits for stream + result)
- renderCall shows 📡 icon for streaming tasks
- HTTP transport: stream=false (streaming would need SSE support)
- Stream buffers cleaned up on session shutdown

Flow:
1. Sender sends task/send with stream=true
2. Receiver processes task, sends content_block_delta as task/stream notifications
3. Sender renders chunks in link-stream widget
4. Receiver sends done=true, then final result
5. Sender clears widget, renders final result as link-result

title: Detect half-open link connections
description:
When a peer session reloads or its link client drops, the other side still reports connected: true. Need heartbeat-based detection: if no ping response within N seconds, mark as disconnected and notify the user.

Symptoms:
- link_status returns connected: true on one side, connected: false on the other
- Tasks sent to a half-open link sit in the socket buffer with no reader
- No error surfaced to the sending agent

Acceptance:
- Periodic ping with timeout (e.g. 10s)
- State transitions: connected → disconnected with event/notice
- Reconnection attempt or clean teardown on detection
